name: FreeClaw
vibe_summary: A minimal Python reimplementation of the OpenClaw concept, focused on free/cheap LLM access via NVIDIA NIM, OpenRouter, and Groq. It ships multi-agent Discord bots, per-agent workspaces, and a task timer, but remains an early, single-maintainer project.
best_for: Users wanting a free OpenClaw-like assistant via NIM/OpenRouter/Groq
Running multiple persona-based Discord bots from one install
Python developers who want a small, hackable agent CLI
avoid_if: You need a mature, battle-tested agent platform
You require strong sandboxing or audited security
You want local model inference (no Ollama-style local backend documented)
openclaw_advantages: Simple Python codebase that is easy to read and modify
Free-tier friendly providers (NIM, Groq, OpenRouter) as defaults
Lightweight multi-agent profiles with per-agent workspaces
Lower resource footprint than the full OpenClaw stack

No documented sandboxing or strong tool isolation
No local model support; requires external API keys

overview_markdown:
FreeClaw is a minimal Python reimplementation of the OpenClaw concept, built around OpenAI-compatible `/v1/chat/completions` endpoints. It defaults to NVIDIA NIM but also supports OpenRouter and Groq, making it oriented toward free or low-cost hosted inference rather than local models. Configuration is environment-variable driven, with tool execution constrained to a configurable `FREECLAW_TOOL_ROOT` and state (persona, tasks, memory DB) stored in per-agent workspaces.

Its standout feature is multi-agent support: each named agent gets its own config, `.env`, memory database, and workspace, and the Discord integration can launch all agent bots at once or a single profile. A task-timer sidecar (with an optional web UI on port 3000) runs scheduled tasks and can post summaries to Discord, and a chat mode allows interaction over SSH.

Compared to OpenClaw, FreeClaw trades the rich ecosystem, polish, and security hardening for a small, approachable Python codebase that is easy to self-host and modify. It is at version 0.1.0 with a single maintainer, no documented sandboxing model, and no community discussion footprint, so it is best suited for tinkerers comfortable with early-stage software.
